questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere where I could study environmental law

questions.answer: I registered online when I applied for the university. Upon arrival the registration was finished when I showed up at the relevant desk with my ID.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: not sure

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite. I got the classes I wanted but they ended up being overlapping so I had to change some classes.

questions.answer: MA

questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was fine compared to the points they were worth.

questions.answer: It's quite the same - a bit less group work at HI than UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Themes of International and European Union Law; Transnational Climate Law; Iceland in the International System; Jury in the US; International Human Rights Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: They were all quite nice!! Interesting subjects :)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Except for having less daylight, life in Reykjavik is not very different than Copenhagen. The city is smaller - so less opportunities but other than that everything was fine! at least 30% of the supermarkets are danish products :)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Show up to events: there is quite a lot events tailored especially for international/erasmus students. Socialise in the beginningen even if its overwhelming - the people i befriended in the beginning are the people I stuck to for the whole semester,

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They have breaks during the movies in the cinema :)). Jokes aside, the most challenging (or annoying) difference have been the heavy reliance on cars for transportation. Nothing is really accessible by public transportation so you need to rent a car or book a guided tour for pretty much any thing :)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything was very tourist friendly (a bit sad, but easy to be a tourist)!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: save up, apply for student housing early and save up a bit more. (+ have a drivings license)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Had some of the most amazing trips in my life so far and met some incredible people!!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Didn't find anything too challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO ON THE TRIPS. MEET NEW PEOPLE. STUDY. Its an amazing opportunity - take it!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
